einzeiler: The decades-long manhunt and eventual capture of family annihilator John List.
kurzfassung: After murdering his family in 1971, John List lived under an assumed name for nearly two decades while evading law enforcement. A broadcast on America's Most Wanted in 1989 ultimately led to a tip that resulted in his arrest and subsequent trial. List was convicted of first-degree murder in 1990 and died in prison in 2008.
stichpunkte: John List murdered his wife, mother, and three children in Westfield, New Jersey, in the winter of 1971.
Following the murders, List vanished, initiating a nationwide manhunt that yielded no progress for nearly twenty years.
List established a new identity as Robert Clark, moving to Colorado and later Virginia, where he remarried and worked as an accountant.
In 1989, police successfully pitched the cold case to the television show America's Most Wanted.
A former neighbor in Colorado recognized the show's age-progression sketch and tipped off the FBI to List's location in Virginia.
Law enforcement agents arrested List in June 1989, confirming his identity through fingerprint records.
During his 1990 trial, the defense argued that List suffered from psychological impairment and religious delusions, claiming he believed the killings were an act of mercy.
A jury rejected the defense's arguments and found List guilty of five counts of first-degree murder, resulting in five consecutive life sentences.
beschreibung:
After killing his family in the winter of 1971, John List went on the run, initiating a worldwide manhunt that would last nearly twenty years before he was finally apprehended. In that time, the List case would become one of the largest and most notorious investigations since the kidnapping of the Lindbergh baby.
